change: Bounded PNG source snapshots as immutable native ImageTexture -> Image resources; bind source bytes through approval/final commit, then embed independent RGBA8 pixels. Not live imported texture references.
upgrade: Explicit host/plugin upgrade: bridge 0.3.5, scene.png_texture/v1, maximum 25 advertised capabilities. Existing frame/file limits, write opt-in and handle quota/TTL unchanged.
contracts: Project-local regular PNG only; reject protected/absolute/traversal/link/junction/hardlink paths. SHA-256 required, 16 KiB maximum, 1..32 dimensions, non-interlaced 8-bit RGB/RGBA, only IHDR/IDAT/IEND.
Host verifies CRC/inflate/scanlines; native decodes exact source bytes and host independently compares every RGBA8 pixel. No importer-cache loading or arbitrary importer provenance claim.

Source-backed handles retain hashes through duplication/read and scene preparation. Combine scene/PNG dependencies within the existing 32-file bound; host rechecks before/after approval and native final commit checks again.

Decline and source changes leave the live document and scene bytes unchanged. Direct export of source-backed handles is refused; approve scene embedding first, then reference/export independent pixels.

Approved embedding is a snapshot, not a live PNG dependency. Removing source afterward preserves native pixels, Undo/Redo, resource export and actual scene save/reopen. External .tres still requires explicit unique embedding.

ImageTexture -> Image storage is bounded RGBA8, no scripts/metadata/mipmaps/compression/size overrides. Generic create only permits an empty-properties 1x1 white default. No in-place texture mutation.

Real post-import native scanning progress 1.85 violated the unchanged strict state schema. Plugin now bounds only the display indicator; real scanning/importing flags and readiness still govern completion.

Actual local imported PNG -> native save -> runtime capture has red/blue pixel samples, >1000 changed pixels on horizontal flip and zero difference after restoring. Not hosted GPU or human UX qualification.
